topic.name: Changing the Order of Integration in Triple Integrals: Changing Projection

exampleAnswers.title: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type

question.text:
The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_0^1\int_0^{1-y^2}\int_0^{2-y-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y \]

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $y,$ and then $z.$
question.explanation:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

\[ R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1-y^2, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 2-y-z \big\} \]

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_a^b\int_{v_1(z)}^{v_2(z)}\int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z \]

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_a^b\int_{v_1(z)}^{v_2(z)}\int_0^{2-y-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $yz$-plane:

\[ D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1-y^2 \big\} \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y$ to $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ is

\[ z=1-y^2 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad y = \sqrt{1-z}. \]

and the left boundary of the region is

\[ y=0. \]

Then, the type II representation of the region $D$ is

\[ D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq \sqrt{1-z} \big\}, \]

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain \[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_0^1 \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{0}}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{ \sqrt{1-z} }} \int_0^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{2-y-z}} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z. \]

question.text:
The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_0^1\int_0^{x^2}\int_0^{x^2+y} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x \]

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y.$
question.explanation:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

\[ R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq x^2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq x^2+y \big\} \]

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y \]

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int_0^{x^2+y} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xy$-plane:

\[ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq x^2 \big\} \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x$ to $\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

\[ y=x^2 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x = \sqrt{y} \]

and the right boundary of the region is

\[ x=1. \]

Then, the type II representation of the region $D$ is

\[ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: \sqrt{y} \leq x \leq 1 \big\}, \]

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain \[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_0^1 \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\sqrt{y}}}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{1}} \int_0^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{x^2+y}} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y. \]

question.text:
The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_0^{2}\int_{ 3-3z/2}^3\int_{8-4x/3-2z}^4 f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z \]

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x.$
question.explanation:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

\[ R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq2, \:\: 3-\dfrac{3z}{2} \leq x \leq 3, \:\: 8-\dfrac{4x}{3} -2z \leq y \leq 4 \right\} \]

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_a^b \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)}\int_{u_1(x,z)}^{u_2(x,z)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x \]

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_a^b\int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)}\int_{8-4x/3-2z}^4 f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xz$-plane:

\[ D = \left\{ (x,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 2, \:\: 3-\dfrac{3z}{2} \leq x \leq 3 \right\} \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z$ to $\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ is

\[ x = 3-\dfrac{3z}{2} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad z = 2-\dfrac{2x}{3} \]

and the top boundary of the region is

\[ z=2. \]

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

\[ D = \left\{ (x,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 3, \:\: 2-\dfrac{2x}{3}\leq z \leq 2 \right\}, \]

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain \[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_0^3 \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{2-2x/3}}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{2}} \int_{8-4/3x-2z}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{4}} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x. \]

question.text:
The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_0^1\int_0^{\sqrt[3]{z}}\int^2_{1+y-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z \]

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$
question.explanation:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

\[ R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq \sqrt[3]{z}, \:\: 1+y-z \leq x \leq 2 \big\} \]

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y \]

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int^2_{1+y-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

\[ D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq {\sqrt[3]{z}} \big\} \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z$ to $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is

\[ y=\sqrt[3]{z} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad z = y^3 \]

and the top boundary of the region is

\[ z=1. \]

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

\[ D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: y^3 \leq z\leq 1 \big\}, \]

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain \[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_0^1 \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{y^3}}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{1}} \int^2_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{1+y-z}} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y. \]

question.text:
The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_{1}^{4}\int_{1}^{4/z}\int_0^{4-yz} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z \]

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$
question.explanation:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

\[ R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 1 \leq z \leq 4, \:\: 1 \leq y \leq \dfrac 4 z, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 4-yz \big\} \]

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y \]

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

\[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int_0^{4-yz} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

\[ D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 1 \leq z \leq 4, \:\: 1 \leq y \leq \dfrac 4 z \big\} \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z$ to $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is

\[ y=\dfrac{4}{z} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad z=\dfrac{4}{y} \]

and the bottom boundary of the region is

\[ z=1. \]

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

\[ D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 1 \leq y \leq 4, \:\: 1 \leq z\leq \dfrac{4}{y} \big\}, \]

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain \[ \iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V = \int_1^4 \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{1}}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{4/y}} \int_0^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{4-yz}} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned

question.text:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $y,$ and then $z,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

\[ \displaystyle \int_{-2}^2 \int_0^{\sqrt{y+2}} \int_{-z}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y + \int_2^6 \int_0^{\sqrt{6-y}} \int_{-z}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y \]
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_a^b \int_{v_1(z)}^{v_2(z)} \int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z. \]

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R = R_1\cup R_2,$ where $R_1$ and $R_2$ are type I regions, is given by

\begin{align*} R_1 &= \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: -2 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq \sqrt{y+2}, \:\: -z \leq x \leq y^2 \right\}, \\[5pt] R_2 &= \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 2 \leq y \leq 6, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq \sqrt{6-y}, \:\: -z \leq x \leq y^2 \right\}. \end{align*}

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

\[ \int_a^b \int_{v_1(z)}^{v_2(z)} \int_{-z}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ consists of two type I regions in the $yz$-plane:

\[ D = \left\{ (y,z) \: : \: -2 \leq y \leq 2, \quad 0 \leq z \leq \sqrt{y+2} \right\} \:\cup\: \left\{ (y,z) \: : \: 2 \leq x \leq 6, \quad 0 \leq z \leq \sqrt{6-y} \right\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y$ to $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ is \[ z=\sqrt{y+2} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad y = z^2-2 \] and the right boundary of the region is \[ z=\sqrt{6-y} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad y = 6-z^2. \]

Then, the type II representation of the region is

\[ D = \left\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 2, \quad z^2-2 \leq y \leq 6-z^2 \right\}, \]

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

\[ \int_0^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{2}} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{z^2-2}}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{6-z^2}} \int_{-z}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z. \]

example.title: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned

question.text:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

\[ \int_0^1 \int_{-z^2-1}^{-z} \int_0^{2y+z} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z = \int_{-2}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{p}} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{q}}^{1} \int_0^{2y+z} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y + \int_{-1}^0 \int_{0}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{r}} \int_0^{2y+z} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y \]
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_a^b \int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)} \int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y + \int_c^d \int_{v_3(y)}^{v_4(y)} \int_{u_3(y,z)}^{u_4(y,z)} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y. \]

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

\[ R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: -z^2-1 \leq y \leq -z, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 2y+z \big\} \]

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

\[ \int_0^1 \int_{-z^2-1}^{-z} \int_0^{2y+z} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z = \int_a^b \int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)} \int_0^{2y+z} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y + \int_c^d \int_{v_3(y)}^{v_4(y)} \int_0^{2y+z} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

\[ D = \big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \quad -z^2-1 \leq y \leq -z \big\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z$ to $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y,$ we split $D$ into two type I regions.

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ are

$\qquad$ $z = \sqrt{-y-1} \quad$ and $\quad z = 1.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ are

$\qquad$ $z = 0 \quad$ and $\quad z = -y.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

\[ D_1 = \big\{ (y,z) \::\: -2 \leq y \leq -1, \quad \sqrt{-y-1} \leq z \leq 1 \big\} \]

and

\[ D_2 = \big\{ (y,z) \::\: -1 \leq y \leq 0, \quad 0 \leq z \leq -y \big\}. \]

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

\begin{align*} \int_{-2}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{-1}} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\sqrt{-y-1}}}^{1} \int_0^{2y+z} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y + \int_{-1}^0 \int_{0}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{-y}} \int_0^{2y+z} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

example.title: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned

question.text:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

\[ \displaystyle \int_0^1 \int_0^{2z} \int_{-y}^{z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z + \int_1^3 \int_0^{3-z} \int_{-y}^{z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z \]
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_a^b \int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)} \int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y. \]

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R = R_1\cup R_2,$ where $R_1$ and $R_2$ are type II regions, is given by

\begin{align*} R_1 &= \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2z, \:\: -y \leq x \leq z \right\}, \\[5pt] R_2 &= \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 1 \leq z \leq 3, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 3-z, \:\: -y \leq x \leq z\right\}. \end{align*}

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

\[ \int_a^b \int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)} \int_{-y}^{z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ consists of two type II regions in the $yz$-plane:

\[ D = \left\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq y \leq 2z \right\} \:\cup\: \left\{ (y,z) \: : \: 1 \leq z \leq 3, \quad 0 \leq y \leq 3-z \right\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z$ to $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is \[ y=2z \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad z =\dfrac{y}{2} \] and the top boundary of the region is \[ y=3-z \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad z = 3-y. \]

Then, the type I representation of the region is

\[ D = \left\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \quad \dfrac{y}{2} \leq z \leq 3-y \right\}, \]

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

\[ \int_0^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{2}} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{y/2}}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{3-y}} \int_{-y}^{z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y. \]

question.text:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

\[ \int_{0}^2 \int_{\sqrt{2y}-1}^{2-y/2} \int_{-2z}^{y+3} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y = \int_{-1}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{p}} \int_{0}^{(z+1)^2/2} \int_{-2z}^{y+3} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z + \int_{1}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{q}} \int_{0}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{r}} \int_{-2z}^{y+3} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z \]
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_a^b \int_{v_1(z)}^{v_2(z)} \int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z + \int_c^d \int_{v_3(z)}^{v_4(z)} \int_{u_3(xy,z)}^{u_4(y,z)} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z. \]

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

\[ R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: \sqrt{2y}-1 \leq z \leq 2-\dfrac{y}{2}, \:\: -2z \leq x \leq y+3 \big\} \]

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

\[ \int_{0}^2 \int_{\sqrt{2y}-1}^{2-y/2} \int_{-2z}^{y+3} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y = \int_a^b \int_{v_1(z)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{-2z}^{y+3} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z + \int_c^d \int_{v_3(z)}^{v_4(x)} \int_{-2z}^{y+3} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $yz$-plane:

\[ D = \left\{ (y,z) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \quad \sqrt{2y}-1 \leq z \leq 2-\dfrac{y}{2} \right\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y$ to $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z,$ we split $D$ into two type II regions.

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ are

$\qquad$ $y = 0 \quad$ and $\quad y = \dfrac{1}{2}(z+1)^2.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ are

$\qquad$ $y = 0 \quad$ and $\quad y = 4-2z.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

\[ D_1 = \left\{ (y,z) \::\: -1 \leq z \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq y \leq \dfrac{1}{2}(z+1)^2 \right\} \]

and

\[ D_2 = \big\{ (y,z) \::\: 1 \leq z \leq 2, \quad 0 \leq x \leq 4-2z \big\}. \]

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

\begin{align*} \int_{-1}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{1}} \int_{0}^{(z+1)^2/2} \int_{-2z}^{y+3} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z + \int_{1}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{2}} \int_{0}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{4-2z}} \int_{-2z}^{y+3} \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z. \end{align*}

question.text:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

\[ \displaystyle \int_{-1}^0 \int_{-2x^3}^{2} \int_{-y}^{x+3} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x + \int_0^2 \int_{\sqrt{2x}}^{2} \int_{-y}^{x+3} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x \]
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_a^b \int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)} \int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y. \]

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R = R_1\cup R_2,$ where $R_1$ and $R_2$ are type I regions, is given by

\begin{align*} R_1 &= \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: -1 \leq x \leq 0, \:\: -2x^3 \leq y \leq 2, \:\: -y \leq z \leq x+3 \right\}, \\[5pt] R_2 &= \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 2, \:\: \sqrt{2x} \leq y \leq 2, \:\: -y \leq z\leq x+3 \right\}. \end{align*}

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

\[ \int_a^b \int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)} \int_{-y}^{x+3} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ consists of two type I regions in the $xy$-plane:

\[ D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: -1 \leq x \leq 0, \quad -2x^3 \leq y \leq 2 \right\} \:\cup\: \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 2, \quad \sqrt{2x} \leq y \leq 2 \right\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x$ to $\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is \[ y=-2x^3 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x = - \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{y}{2}} \] and the right boundary of the region is \[ y=\sqrt{2x} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x = \dfrac{1}{2}y^2. \]

Then, the type II representation of the region is

\[ D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \quad -\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{y}{2}} \leq x \leq \dfrac{1}{2}y^2 \right\}, \]

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

\[ \int_0^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{2}} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{-\sqrt[3]{y/2}}}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{y^2/2}} \int_{-y}^{x+3} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y. \]

question.text:
Evaluate $ \displaystyle \int_{0}^{1} \int_{\arcsin{y}}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\cos{z}} \sqrt{1 + \cos^2{z}} \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y. $

Hint: First change the order of integration to $\textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z.$
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(z)}^{v_2(z)} \int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} \sqrt{1 + \cos^2{z}} \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z. \]

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows: \[ R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: \arcsin{y} \leq z \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq \cos{z} \right\} \]

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before: \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(z)}^{v_2(z)} \int_{0}^{\cos{z}} \sqrt{1 + \cos^2{z}} \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is type I region in the $yz$-plane: \[ D = \left\{ (y,z) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \quad \arcsin{y} \leq z \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2} \right\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y$ to $\textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is \[ y = 0 \] and the right boundary of the region $D,$ written in the form $y = y(z),$ is \[ z = \arcsin{y} \qquad\Longrightarrow \qquad y = \sin{z}. \]

Then, the type II representation of the region is \[ D = \left\{ (y,z) \::\: 0 \leq z \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \quad 0 \leq y \leq \sin{z} \right\}, \]

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain \begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{\arcsin{y}}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\cos{z}} \sqrt{1 + \cos^2{z}} \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y & = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\sin{z}} \int_{0}^{\cos{z}} \sqrt{1 + \cos^2{z}} \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z\\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\sin{z}} \left[ \sqrt{1 + \cos^2{z}}\int_{0}^{\cos{z}} \textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\sin{z}} \sqrt{1 + \cos^2{z}} \: \big[ x \big]_{0}^{\cos{z}} \: \textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\sin{z}} \cos{z}\sqrt{1 + \cos^2{z}} \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \left[ \cos{z}\sqrt{1 + \cos^2{z}} \int_{0}^{\sin{z}} \textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}z \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos{z}\sqrt{1 + \cos^2{z}} \: \big[y\big]_{0}^{\sin{z}} \:\textrm{d}z \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin{z}\cos{z}\sqrt{1 + \cos^2{z}} \: \textrm{d}z \\[5pt] %&= \dfrac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi/2} 2\sin{z}\cos{z}\sqrt{1 + \cos^2{z}} \: \textrm{d}z \\[5pt] & =\left[-\dfrac{1}{3}\left(1 + \cos^2{z}\right)^{3/2}\right]_{0}^{\pi/2}\\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{1}{3}\left[(1+0)^{3/2} - (1+1)^{3/2}\right]\\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{1}{3}\left(1 - 2^{3/2}\right)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2} - 1}{3}. \end{align*}

question.text:
Evaluate $ \displaystyle \int_{0}^{1} \int_{\sqrt{z}}^{1} \int_{0}^{e^{\large z/x}} \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z. $

Hint: First change the order of integration to $\textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x.$
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{u_1(x,z)}^{u_2(x,z)} \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x. \]

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows: \[ R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: \sqrt{z} \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq e^{z/x} \right\} \]

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before: \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{0}^{e^{\large z/x}} \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is type II region in the $xz$-plane: \[ D = \left\{ (x,z) \::\: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \quad \sqrt{z} \leq x \leq 1 \right\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z$ to $\textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region $D,$ written in the form $z = z(x),$ is \[ x = \sqrt{z} \qquad\Longrightarrow \qquad z = x^2 \] and the bottom boundary of the region $D$ is \[ z = 0. \]

Then, the type I representation of the region is \[ D = \left\{ (x,z) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq z \leq x^2 \right\}, \]

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain \begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{\sqrt{z}}^{1} \int_{0}^{e^{\large z/x}} \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z & = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{x^2} \int_{0}^{e^{\large z/x}} \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{x^2} \left[ \int_{0}^{e^{\large z/x}} \textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{x^2} \big[ y \big]_{0}^{e^{\large z/x}} \: \textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{x^2} e^{z/x} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \left[ \int_{0}^{x^2} e^{z/x} \: \textrm{d}z \right] \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \big[ xe^{z/x} \big]_{z=0}^{z=x^2} \:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} (xe^{x} - x) \: \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \left[ (x-1)e^{x} - \dfrac{1}{2}x^2 \right]_{0}^{1} \\[5pt] & =\left(0 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) - (-1 - 0)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*}

question.text:
Evaluate $ \displaystyle \int_{0}^{1} \int_{\arcsin{y}}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{e^{\large \cos{x}}} \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y. $

Hint: First change the order of integration to $\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x.$
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)} \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x. \]

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows: \[ R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: \arcsin{y} \leq x \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq e^{\cos{x}} \right\} \]

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before: \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{0}^{e^{\large \cos{x}}} \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is type II region in the $xy$-plane: \[ D = \left\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \quad \arcsin{y} \leq x \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2} \right\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y$ to $\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $y = y(x),$ is \[ x = \arcsin{y} \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad y = \sin{x} \]

and the bottom boundary of the region $D$ is \[ y = 0. \]

Then, the type I representation of the region is \[ D = \left\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \quad 0 \leq y \leq \sin{x} \right\}, \]

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{\arcsin{y}}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{e^{\large \cos{x}}} \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y & = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\sin{x}} \int_{0}^{e^{\large \cos{x}}} \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\sin{x}} \left[ \int_{0}^{e^{\large \cos{x}}} \textrm{d}z \right] \textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\sin{x}} \big[ z \big]_{0}^{e^{\large \cos{x}}} \: \textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\sin{x}} e^{\cos{x}} \: \textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} e^{\cos{x}} \left[ \int_{0}^{\sin{x}} \textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} e^{\cos{x}} \big[ y \big]_{0}^{\sin{x}} \:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} e^{\cos{x}}\sin{x} \:\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \big[ -e^{\cos{x}} \big]_{0}^{\pi/2} \\[5pt] & = -\left(e^{\cos{\pi/2}}-e^{\cos{0}} \right) \\[5pt] & = -(1 - e)\\[5pt] & = e-1. \end{align*}

question.text:
Evaluate $ \displaystyle \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{\arccos{y}} \int_{0}^{2} y \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y. $

Hint: First change the order of integration to $\textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z.$
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(z)}^{v_2(z)} \int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} y \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z. \]

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows: \[ R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq \arccos{y}, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq 2 \right\} \]

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before: \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(z)}^{v_2(z)} \int_{0}^{2} y \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is type I region in the $yz$-plane: \[ D = \left\{ (y,z) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq z \leq \arccos{y} \right\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y$ to $\textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is \[ y = 0 \] and the right boundary of the region $D,$ written in the form $y = y(z),$ is \[ z = \arccos{y} \qquad\Longrightarrow \qquad y = \cos{z}. \]

Then, the type II representation of the region is \[ D = \left\{ (y,z) \::\: 0 \leq z \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \quad 0 \leq y \leq \cos{z} \right\}, \]

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain \begin{align*} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{\arccos{y}} \int_{0}^{2} y \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y & = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\cos{z}} \int_{0}^{2} y \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z\\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\cos{z}} \left[ \int_{0}^{2} y\, \textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\cos{z}} y \: \big[ x \big]_{0}^{2} \: \textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{0}^{\cos{z}} 2y \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \left[ \int_{0}^{\cos{z}} 2y \: \textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}z \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \big[y^2\big]_{0}^{\cos{z}} \:\textrm{d}z \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^2{z} \: \textrm{d}z \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{1}{2}(1 + \cos{2z}) \: \textrm{d}z \\[5pt] %&= \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{0}^{\pi/2} (1 + \cos{2z}) \: \textrm{d}z \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[z + \dfrac{1}{2}\sin{2z}\right]_{0}^{\pi/2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\pi}{4}. \end{align*}

question.text:
Evaluate $ \displaystyle \int_{1}^{e} \int_{\ln{z}}^{1} \int_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y} \dfrac{y}{x^2 + y^2} \,\textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z. $

Hint: First change the order of integration to $\textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y.$
question.explanation:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)} \int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} \dfrac{y}{x^2 + y^2} \, \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y. \]

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows: \[ R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 1 \leq z \leq e, \:\: \ln{z} \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq \sqrt{3}y \right\} \]

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before: \[ \int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)} \int_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y} \dfrac{y}{x^2 + y^2} \, \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \]

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

The region $D$ is type II region in the $yz$-plane: \[ D = \left\{ (y,z) \::\: 1 \leq z \leq e, \quad \ln{z} \leq y \leq 1 \right\}. \]

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z$ to $\textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region $D$ is \[ z = 1 \] and the top boundary of the region $D,$ written in the form $z = z(y),$ is \[ y = \ln{z} \qquad\Longrightarrow \qquad z = e^{y}. \]

Then, the type I representation of the region is \[ D = \left\{ (y,z) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \quad 1 \leq z \leq e^{y} \right\}, \]

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain \begin{align*} \int_{1}^{e} \int_{\ln{z}}^{1} \int_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y} \dfrac{y}{x^2 + y^2} \,\textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}z & = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{1}^{e^{y}} \int_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y} \dfrac{y}{x^2 + y^2} \, \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y\\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \int_{1}^{e^{y}} \left[ \int_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y} \dfrac{y}{x^2 + y^2} \, \textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{1}^{e^{y}} \left[ \arctan\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right) \right]_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{3}y} \: \textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{1}^{e^{y}} \arctan{\sqrt{3}} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] & = \int_{0}^{1} \int_{1}^{e^{y}} \dfrac{\pi}{3} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \left[ \dfrac{\pi}{3} \int_{1}^{e^{y}} \textrm{d}z \right] \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{\pi}{3}\big[z\big]_{1}^{e^{y}} \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{1} \dfrac{\pi}{3}(e^{y} - 1) \: \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] %& = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\int_{0}^{1} (e^y - 1) \: \textrm{d}y\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\big[e^{y} - y\big]_{0}^{1}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\left(e - 1 - 1+0\right)\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\pi(e-2)}{3}. \end{align*}
